bug_classes.blocks_question: Why did this request fail (which trace/request was it)?
bug_classes.definition: An event classified as a failure (error/critical severity, or an ok/status/success field indicating failure) that carries no correlation identifier (trace_id, traceId, request_id, span_id, or a recognised alias).
bug_classes.false_positive_sources: An event mislabelled as a failure (heuristic severity inference), or a correlation id embedded inside a composite/nested field we do not flatten.
bug_classes.guarantee: If reported, the sampled failure event provably lacks any recognised correlation field, so it cannot be joined to a distributed trace or request timeline from the telemetry alone.
bug_classes.incompleteness: A clean result only covers sampled events and recognised correlation aliases; a correlation id under an unrecognised key, or failures not present in the sampled data, are not detected.
bug_classes.title: Failure without correlation id

bug_classes.blocks_question: How long did this operation take?
bug_classes.definition: An event whose kind is span/spans that carries no duration measure (duration_ms, duration, elapsed_ms, latency_ms, or a recognised alias).
bug_classes.false_positive_sources: A non-span event misclassified as a span by kind inference.
bug_classes.guarantee: If reported, the sampled span provably lacks any recognised duration field, so latency cannot be computed from the span alone.
bug_classes.incompleteness: Only events whose kind is inferred as a span are considered; spans mislabelled as plain events, or duration recoverable from separate start/end timestamps, are not detected.
bug_classes.title: Span without duration

bug_classes.definition: A failure event that carries no error code, exception type, or status evidence field (error_code, exception, exception_type, status, status_code, or a recognised alias).
bug_classes.false_positive_sources: A mislabelled failure, or error detail present only in an unstructured message field.
bug_classes.guarantee: If reported, the sampled failure event provably lacks any recognised error-evidence field, so its root cause is not recoverable from the event itself.
bug_classes.incompleteness: Only sampled failures and recognised evidence aliases are covered; error detail carried in a free-text message we do not parse is not credited.
bug_classes.title: Failure without error evidence

bug_classes.blocks_question: Is this telemetry safe to retain and share?
bug_classes.definition: A scalar field whose value matches a high-precision raw-secret/PII pattern (email, bearer token, JWT, password assignment, or a card/phone value in a card/phone-named field).
bug_classes.false_positive_sources: A synthetic/example value (e.g. test fixtures) that matches the pattern but is not real production data.
bug_classes.guarantee: If reported, the sampled value matches a deliberately conservative raw-secret/PII pattern, indicating unredacted sensitive data is present in telemetry.
bug_classes.incompleteness: Patterns are tuned for precision over recall; obfuscated, encoded, or domain-specific secrets, and secrets in unsampled events, are not detected.
bug_classes.title: Raw sensitive value in telemetry

bug_classes.blocks_question: Will this metric explode storage / cost as it scales?
bug_classes.definition: A metric label whose distinct-value count across the sampled points is high relative to the sample (sample-size gated), indicating likely unbounded cardinality.
bug_classes.false_positive_sources: A bounded label that happens to be near-unique within a small sample.
bug_classes.guarantee: If reported, the sampled metric label exhibits a distinct-value ratio consistent with unbounded cardinality at scale.
bug_classes.incompleteness: Gated on sample size; labels that are unbounded only beyond the sampled window are not detected, and bursty-but-bounded labels may be flagged.
bug_classes.title: Unbounded metric label cardinality

bug_classes.blocks_question: Which fields carry regulated or tenant-scoped data?
bug_classes.definition: A field whose name indicates a tenant/customer/account/user identifier or sensitive attribute, emitted without redaction/hashing and without a privacy classification.
bug_classes.false_positive_sources: A field whose name resembles a sensitive identifier but whose value is non-sensitive (e.g. a public account slug).
bug_classes.guarantee: If reported, a field named like a sensitive/tenant identifier is emitted in the clear with no declared privacy handling.
bug_classes.incompleteness: Name-based; a sensitive field with an innocuous name is not flagged, and a benign field with a sensitive-looking name may be.
bug_classes.title: Unclassified sensitive / tenant identifier

rules.remediation: Emit one of the layer-local alternative evidence paths.
Attach the field required by the layer-local assume-guarantee obligation.
Assign the layer owner and emit the signal required by the assume-guarantee obligation.
Emit a witness whose field value satisfies the layer-local predicate.
Provide the minimum observations needed by the assigned incident-response layer.
Preserve the temporal property assigned to this layer.
Document or remove collector/exporter transformations observed in the finite trace.
Declare allowed_values as an array.
Declare each alternative obligation with an id and a non-empty any_of list of signal options.
Declare assume-guarantee obligations under service_guarantees, collector_assumptions, environment_assumptions, or oncall_obligations with concrete finite-trace evidence.
Declare conditional requirements with an if field condition and then fields list.
Declare each field name in only one of fields, attributes, or tags for a signal.
Keep one contract definition per signal name and kind.
Declare reusable field definitions as an object of field specs.
Reference an existing field definition or inline the field spec.
Remove cyclic field-definition references.
Use one of string, integer, number, boolean, object, array, or null.
Declare forbidden_patterns as a string, object, or array of strings/objects.
Declare hyperproperties with a valid type, witness fields, and pair/set quantification keys.
Fix the regular expression in the contract.
Declare min and max bounds as numbers.
Ensure min is less than or equal to max.
Declare sampling and retention policy stubs with machine-readable rates, strategies, and day counts.
Declare a known privacy classification and an allowed transformation such as redacted, hashed, tokenized, bucketed, or omitted.
Use a boolean for required flags.
Update the contract so it conforms to docs/contract.schema.json.
Use arrays for spans, metrics, and logs sections.
Classify sensitive fields with sensitivity and forbid raw-secret patterns.
Add a non-empty service name.
Use a known log severity threshold such as WARN, ERROR, or FATAL.
Give each signal a stable telemetry name.
Describe each signal as an object.
Declare strict-validation escape hatches as bounded service, signal, field, or transformation lists.
Declare temporal properties with a valid type, selectors, predicates, grouping keys, and positive time bounds.
Declare temporal sequences with valid steps, kinds, group_by keys, and positive windows.
Use a supported unit such as ms, bytes, percent, count, timestamp_ms, or usd.
Declare contract version 1.0.
Review changed incident-question, temporal, alternative, or preservation claims against real fixtures.
Review the new telemetry obligation and ensure fixtures, owners, and rollout plans cover it.
Review privacy-classification or transformation changes with the data owner before merging.
Confirm that removing the telemetry obligation is intentional and does not regress incident diagnosability.
Attach an error code, exception type/stack, or status to failure events so incidents are diagnosable from the data you already emit.
Fix the referenced input path or file format.
Inspect collector/exporter dropped-count fields before relying on complete contract evidence.
Fix or exclude malformed OTLP JSONL records before asserting full export coverage.
Prefer canonical OTLP JSON field names, or keep alias normalization diagnostics with the import artifact.
Fix malformed OTLP containers or unsupported item shapes so importer semantics are complete.
Add importer support or avoid the unsupported metric encoding before making metric-contract claims.
Document unsupported top-level OTLP fields as validity threats or add bounded importer support.
Change or configure the transformation so transformed telemetry still satisfies obligations that held before transformation.
Keep the transformed field, or provide an approved surrogate that still answers the selected incident question.
Keep at least one transformed signal witness for each selected diagnosability requirement.
Do not add harder collector, environment, on-call, sampling, or retention assumptions in a refining contract.
Change the candidate predicate to be equal to or stronger than the inherited base predicate.
Lint both contracts before comparing refinement.
Keep inherited privacy classifications, sensitivity, and allowed transformation sets at least as restrictive.
Keep every required base field required in the candidate contract.
Keep every required base signal, scenario, temporal property, alternative obligation, and service guarantee required in the candidate.
Compare contracts for the same service or declare an organization/team refinement scope.
Keep strict closed-world validation enabled and avoid adding new escape hatches in the candidate.
Do not approve new transformations or drop inherited preservation scenarios unless the base policy is changed first.
Emit one alternative observation that can answer the scenario question.
Emit the field needed to answer the scenario question.
Emit the signal needed to answer the scenario question.
Add or select a scenario that matches the incident question.
Describe scenario requirements as objects.
Rename the legacy attribute to the cited current OpenTelemetry semantic-convention attribute.
Satisfy the contract's metadata.semantic_conventions local policy or update the policy with a bounded justification.
Declare the metric unit explicitly and consider removing the unit-only suffix from the metric name.
Add the cited OpenTelemetry semantic-convention attribute to the contract and emitted telemetry, or document an artifact-scoped local exception.
Rename the signal to the cited low-cardinality OpenTelemetry semantic-convention shape.
Attach a bounded retryable value when the contract requires retry guidance.
Declare the metric description in the OpenTelemetry metric API call.
Declare the metric unit in the OpenTelemetry metric API call.
Include a trace_id, request_id, or configured correlation field in error logs.
Set the OpenTelemetry span status to ERROR on error paths.
Record caught exceptions on error spans so incident responders can inspect failure type and stack context.
Add source instrumentation with the expected stable telemetry name.
Initialize the OpenTelemetry meter with the expected instrumentation scope name.
Attach a bounded remediation hint on error spans or logs when the contract requires operator guidance.
Attach the required semantic-convention attribute in source instrumentation.
Initialize the OpenTelemetry tracer with the expected instrumentation scope name.
Pass source files or directories to the static checker.
Remove PII or tenant/customer identifiers from logs, or emit redacted/hash/bucketed surrogates.
Remove the sensitive value from logs or log only a redacted/hash surrogate.
Avoid user-controlled/high-cardinality metric labels or add bucketing.
Replace raw payload/body previews with allowlisted sanitized previews or omit them.
Normalize the field to one of the declared allowed values.
Emit at least one of the declared alternative evidence options with its required fields.
Bucket, hash, drop, or bound labels with excessive cardinality.
Declare a max cardinality or explicitly allow unbounded values.
When the triggering field is present, emit all fields required by the conditional requirement.
Propagate at least one shared correlation key value across the required signal kinds.
Emit a trace_id, span_id, request_id, or configured correlation key on correlated signals.
Emit the field using the contract's declared primitive type.
Redact, hash, or omit values matching forbidden sensitive patterns.
Redact, hash, tokenize, bucket, or omit sensitive values before they reach public telemetry sinks.
Do not allow telemetry for different tenants to share an isolation key such as trace_id, request_id, or session_id.
Use a stable log message or event name matching the contract.
Emit the log at the severity required for alerting and search.
Raise the emitted log severity to meet the contract's minimum severity policy.
Attach the required attribute/tag/field to the signal.
Emit the required span, metric, or log on the exercised path.
Investigate or clamp values above the declared maximum.
Investigate or clamp values below the declared minimum.
Normalize the field so it matches the declared pattern.
Emit a string value when a regex pattern is required.
Emit the field using the transformation required by the contract privacy policy.
Classify the field sensitivity and redact or hash the emitted value.
Do not emit raw PII, credentials, or bearer tokens in telemetry.
Declare the emitted signal in spans, metrics, logs, scenarios, or alternative obligations, or add an explicit strict allow_undeclared_signals escape hatch.
Document the collector transformation under metadata.transformation_preservation.approved_transformations or strict allow_collector_transformations.
Declare the emitted field on the signal contract or add an explicit strict allowed_extra_fields escape hatch.
Either emit telemetry for the modeled service or add a bounded allow_unmodeled_services escape hatch.
Do not emit the forbidden event in traces covered by this absence property.
Emit the deadline-bound event before the declared time budget expires.
Emit every event required by the temporal sequence in the grouped incident window.
Emit telemetry in the order required by the temporal property or sequence.
Emit the required response event inside the bounded response window after each trigger.
Keep every matched event inside the declared temporal invariant.
Emit the temporal sequence within the declared bounded window.
Emit a value that satisfies the field's declared unit constraints.

semantics.bug_class: The observability bug class this finding witnesses (see bug_classes); null when the rule is not part of the headline bug-class taxonomy.
semantics.ci_mapping: default_fail_on is the minimum severity a CI gate may use for this rule; sarif_level maps directly to SARIF result.level.
semantics.finding: A finite witness that one telemetry-contract obligation failed or needs operator attention.
semantics.formal_clause: Stable identifier for the well-formedness, satisfaction, adequacy, preservation, static, or input rule that justifies the finding.
